caveats: NASA POWER irradiance/wind is native ~0.5-1 deg: only 16 sample points, cell values are smooth interpolation, ridge-top wind NOT resolved (Global Wind Atlas would be the upgrade).
Slope-share and land-use share are multiplied as if independent.
Substation distance is a straight-line proxy; no capacity, voltage-level or land-ownership data.

weights.src: assumption: usable share of land-cover class (60 bare, 30 grass, 20 shrub, 40 cropland); cropland is low because buying farmland is slow and costly

max_slope_deg.src: assumption: ground-mount PV rule of thumb, flat to gentle terrain

ha_per_mw.src: assumption: brief range 1.6-2.0 ha/MW for Indian utility PV. Cross-check: Pavagada 13,000 acres / 2,050 MW = 2.57 ha/MW gross incl. roads and substations (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavagada_Solar_Park, 2024)

solar.cuf_formula: CUF = GHI[kWh/m2/day] * 365 * PR / 8760 per kWp at 1 kW/m2 STC (DC basis, no inverter clipping or degradation)

tariff_rs_kwh.src: assumption: SECI standalone ISTS solar tranches ~Rs 2.57-2.60/kWh (https://www.constructionworld.in/energy-infrastructure/power-and-renewable-energy/cerc-approves-tariff-for-secis-1.2-gw-solar-projects/70290 , 2025). Solar+storage auctions are higher (Rs 2.86, https://www.pv-magazine.com/2025/10/16/indias-solar-plus-storage-tender-sets-record-low-inr-2-86-tariff/ , Oct 2025) and are not used

capex_cr_per_mw.src: Government of India stated Rs 3.5-4 crore/MW utility solar (Sept 2025, as cited in https://avaadaelectro.com/blog/solar-power-plant-setup-cost-india/ ); examples Rs 3.82 cr/MW UP 209 MW (Oct 2025) and Rs 3.5 cr/MW SJVN Rajasthan 100 MW (Jan 2025); UERC benchmark Rs 3.08 cr/MW from 1 Apr 2025 (low case, https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3cf05968255451bdefe3c5bc64d550517/uploads/2025/06/202506131910199470.pdf); LinkedIn 2025 EPC range Rs 3.1-4.2 cr/MW (high case). Base 3.7 = mid of government range. Not tuned to results. Excludes land. Capex is per MW DC (CUF is DC basis)

grid_cr_per_km.src: assumption: ~Rs 0.8 crore/km for a 66-132 kV evacuation line, unverified; charged once per cell on distance to nearest substation

min_project_mw.src: assumption: cells below 20 MW usable are not ranked (too small for a utility project alone)

wacc.src: assumption: WACC 9-10% (mid 9.5%) typical for Indian utility RE debt+equity, not verified against a single document

life_yr.src: assumption: 25-year project life, standard PPA term. CRF = w/(1-(1+w)^-n) = 0.106

road_cr_per_km.src: assumption: ~Rs 0.5 crore/km new heavy-haul access road (6-7 m, compacted), unverified

t_cell_rise_c.src: assumption: module temperature = annual-mean T2M + 20 C (operating rise at sun, simple approximation; overstates annual mean since night hours are cooler, so derate is conservative)

temp_coeff_per_c.src: assumption: crystalline-Si power temperature coefficient -0.4 %/C (typical datasheet); applied above 25 C. PR 0.77 treated as the 25 C-module reference

cluster_lcoe_factor.src: assumption: 'suitable' for clustering = ranked and LCOE <= 1.20 x tariff (Rs 3.12/kWh solar). Raised from 1.10 because the best solar cell is Rs 2.98 and no cell is viable at base capex; blocks are therefore 'near-viable', not viable

block_mw.src: assumption: developers want contiguous blocks >= 50 MW (user brief)

weights.src: assumption: wind coexists with farming/rangeland, so full weight; built, water, wetland, mangrove, >50% tree excluded

min_ws50.src: assumption: brief threshold 5.5-6 m/s at 50 m; cells below are not ranked

mw_per_km2.src: assumption: brief range 5-8 MW/km2 of developable land. NREL (Denholm et al. 2009, https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy09osti/45834.pdf) reports ~3 MW/km2 total-area for US farms; the Indian figure is the brief's, unverified

hub_alpha.src: assumption: power-law shear exponent 1/7, WS50M scaled to 100 m hub: x (100/50)^alpha

power_curve.src: assumption: generic 3 MW class turbine, cubic ramp cut-in to rated; wind speed Rayleigh distributed with mean = hub speed

min_project_mw.src: assumption: one turbine-class cluster; a 1 km cell holds at most ~6-8 MW, so neighbours would be aggregated in practice

wacc.src: assumption: WACC 9-10% (mid 9.5%) typical for Indian utility RE debt+equity, not verified against a single document

life_yr.src: assumption: 25-year project life, standard PPA term. CRF = w/(1-(1+w)^-n) = 0.106

wind.status: not viable in this box at 0.5 deg resolution; Karnataka's wind belt is the Chitradurga/Gadag ridges; Global Wind Atlas is the upgrade

road_cr_per_km.src: assumption: as solar; wind distance uses primary/secondary/trunk/motorway only because blade transport needs them

cluster_lcoe_factor.src: assumption: 'suitable' for clustering = ranked and LCOE <= 1.20 x tariff (Rs 3.12/kWh solar). Raised from 1.10 because the best solar cell is Rs 2.98 and no cell is viable at base capex; blocks are therefore 'near-viable', not viable

tree_frac.src: assumption: brief; cell excluded if tree cover (WorldCover 10) > 50%

unusable_frac.src: assumption: cell excluded if water+wetland+built+mangrove > 50%, or protected area > 50%

flood_occurrence_pct.src: assumption (user brief): pixels with JRC Global Surface Water occurrence > 5% are excluded; cell usable area scaled by (1 - flooded share), cell excluded if flooded share > 50%

sources.irradiance_wind: NASA POWER climatology API, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN and WS50M annual (2001-2025), https://power.larc.nasa.gov/ , coarse: native ~0.5-1 deg grid
sources.slope: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2021) COGs, https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com/ , resampled to 25 m
sources.grid_osm: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API (power=line, power=substation, solar, protected areas), fetched 2026, ODbL
sources.flood_water: JRC Global Surface Water occurrence v1.4 (2021 release), https://storage.googleapis.com/global-surface-water/downloads2021/occurrence/occurrence_70E_20Nv1_4_2021.tif ; water for cleaning = km to nearest OSM natural=water/waterway or JRC occurrence > 50% (info only)
sources.temperature: NASA POWER T2M annual climatology, same API as irradiance

pavagada_park.note: Cells with >=25% inside OSM solar polygons. Second row waives the 'built' exclusion/weight on those cells because WorldCover 2021 may label panels as built; this is applied to park cells only.

other_osm_solar.note: Cells holding OSM solar generators (points/small ways) outside the park cells; small n, mapping is patchy.

sensitivity.note: Ranking is by LCOE so tariff does not change the order, only which cells are viable (LCOE < tariff).

validation.pavagada_lcoe_percentiles_note: percentile = share of ranked cells with higher LCOE

vs_previous_run.note: measured manually in the run before this one (LCOE ranking before access road, heat derate, flood exclusion); the script cannot recompute it once the report is overwritten
